Agreements
Please read this important information
By completing this enrollment form, I agree to the following:
If I am enrolling in a Medicare Advantage health plan that has a contract with the federal government, I must keep both
Hospital Part A and Medical Part B to stay in Humana Gold Plus - Diabetes and Heart (HMO C-SNP). I must continue to pay
my Medicare Part B premium. It is my responsibility to inform Humana Inc. of any prescription drug coverage that I have or
coverage (as good as Medicare’s), I may have to pay a late enrollment penalty if I enroll in Medicare prescription drug
coverage in the future. With few exceptions, I can only be in one Medicare Advantage health plan or Medicare prescription
drug plan at a time. I understand that my enrollment in my selected plan may end my enrollment in another Medicare
Advantage health plan or prescription drug plan. Enrollment in my selected plan is generally for the entire year.
Humana Inc., I have the right to appeal plan decisions about payment or services if I disagree.

This Humana Inc. plan serves a specific service area. If I move out of the area that my selected plan serves, I need to notify
Humana Inc. so I can disenroll and find a new plan in my new area. I understand that Medicare beneficiaries are generally
Once Humana Inc. has received my enrollment form, I may get a verification letter to make sure that I understand how my
plan works and to confirm my intent to enroll. This is not a secondary plan to Medicare Parts A and B. Humana Inc. pays
coinsurances. Medicare Parts A and B won’t pay for my healthcare while I am enrolled in Humana Inc..
If you are requesting membership in a Private Fee For Service (PFFS) plan, the following statement applies: I understand
that this plan is a Medicare Advantage PFFS plan which may have prescription drug coverage built in. Before seeing a
provider, I should verify that the provider will accept this plan before each visit. My doctor or hospital isn’t required to
agree to accept the plan’s terms and conditions, and thus may choose not to treat me, except for emergencies. I understand
that my healthcare providers have the right to choose whether to accept a PFFS plan’s payment terms and conditions every
time I see them. I understand that if my provider decides not to accept PFFS, I will need to find another provider that will. I
understand that if my PFFS plan doesn’t offer Medicare prescription drug coverage, I may obtain coverage from another
Medicare prescription drug plan.Once I enroll, I may leave this plan or make changes only at certain times of the year if an
enrollment period is available (Example: Annual Enrollment Period from October 15 – December 7 of every year), or under
certain special circumstances.If you are requesting membership in a Private Fee For Service (PFFS) plan, the following
statement applies: Once Humana Gold Plus - Diabetes and Heart (HMO C-SNP) has your enrollment form, you will get a
call from a plan representative. This call is to make sure that you understand how a Private Fee-for-Service plan works and
to confirm your intent to enroll in Humana Gold Plus - Diabetes and Heart (HMO C-SNP). If Humana Gold Plus - Diabetes
and Heart (HMO C-SNP) isn’t able to reach you by telephone, then you will get a letter by mail that contains similar
information.If you are requesting membership in a Private Fee For Service (PFFS) plan, the following statement applies: As
a Medicare Private Fee-For-Service plan, Humana Gold Plus - Diabetes and Heart (HMO C-SNP) works differently than a
Medicare supplement plan as well as other Medicare Advantage plans. Humana Gold Plus - Diabetes and Heart (HMO C-
SNP) pays instead of Medicare, and I will be responsible for the amounts that Humana Gold Plus - Diabetes and Heart
(HMO C-SNP) doesn’t cover, such as copayments and coinsurances. Original Medicare won’t pay for my health care while I
am enrolled in Humana Gold Plus - Diabetes and Heart (HMO C-SNP).
Effect on Current Coverage. If you are currently enrolled in a Medicare Advantage plan, your current Medicare Advantage
Medigap plan, once your Medicare Advantage coverage starts, you may want to drop your Medigap policy because you will
be paying for coverage you cannot use.
Your response to this form is voluntary. However, failure to respond may affect enrollment in the plan.
